title: Run of Show — Benchmark Report Launch Webinar (Latency/$ in Production)
content:
Webinar: Benchmark Report Launch — “Latency/$ in Production: What We Measured and How to Use It”

Last updated: 2025-07-08 (for rehearsal + live)
Owner/producer: Noura El-Khoury
PMM/approval: Soojin Lee
Legal review partner: Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes (claims language + required disclaimers)

---
1) Summary

Goal
- Explain Redwood’s new public benchmark report focused on production inference economics (latency/$) and give attendees a concrete way to interpret the results.
- Drive 2 conversion paths:
  (A) Self-serve: start a Hosted API trial + use the interactive benchmark page
  (B) Sales-assisted: request Dedicated sizing / Private (VPC/on-prem) consult for predictable throughput + residency/security

Primary audience
- Engineers and ML engineers evaluating inference providers
- Platform teams comparing regions / deployment modes
- Solutions architects looking for methodology + reproducibility details

Webinar format
- 45 minutes total (35 min presentation + 10 min Q&A)
- Live demo of interactive benchmark page + “how we measured” highlights

Hard constraints (do not deviate)
- Do not claim “fastest” or “cheapest” universally. Always qualify: “in our measured workloads and configurations” and point to methodology.
- Do not imply competitor internal costs/pricing unless sourced and caveated.
- Do not share sensitive operational details (customer IDs, internal hostnames, fleet topology beyond what’s already public).

---
2) Logistics

Date/time
- Target: Launch week (confirm with PMM): Wed 2025-07-09 @ 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 19:00 CET

Platform
- Zoom Webinar (Marketing Ops to confirm link + registration)
- Stream to YouTube: NO (for this launch; keep Q&A manageable)

Recording
- Record to cloud
- Post within 24 hours to registrants + Redwood docs/blog page

Moderator duties (Noura)
- Start recording
- Read housekeeping + disclaimers
- Keep time, transition speakers, manage questions in chat/Q&A
- Trigger backup plan if demo is slow (screenshots + preloaded CSV)

Support roles during live
- Chat/Q&A triage: Ben Carter (routing + common questions), Markus Klein (SE-level questions)
- Tech monitor: Sean Gallagher (page performance + contingency call)
- Analytics: Logan Wright (verify events fire: webinar CTA link clicks, benchmark page visits)

---
3) Speaker lineup + responsibilities

Host / Moderator
- Noura El-Khoury (Community/Events)
  - Housekeeping, speaker intros, Q&A moderation, closing CTA

Story + positioning
- Soojin Lee (Director of Product Marketing)
  - Why latency/$ matters; how to use the report; what decisions it helps with

Methodology
- Claire Dubois (Sr Research Engineer)
  - Workload definitions, prompt set philosophy, concurrency, warmups, caching policy (as published), variance/stability

Results + interpretation
- Jonas Weber (Dir Performance & Evals)
  - Key takeaways; how to read p50/p95 vs latency/$; region consistency; common pitfalls

Demo
- Felix Schneider (Interactive web tables/filters engineer)
  - Walkthrough of interactive benchmark page: filters, metric toggles, export, disclaimers/tooltips

Optional (only if time allows)
- Ethan Wallace (Content Marketing)
  - Where to find the PDF + blog + methodology appendix; how to share internally

---
4) Slide + demo assets checklist

Slides (Deck owner: Soojin / Alicia)
- Title slide + agenda
- “Why latency/$” framing
- What’s included in the benchmark (models/regions/workloads overview)
- Methodology highlights (what we controlled vs what varies)
- Results: 2–3 hero charts (latency/$ by model+region; p95 heatmap; $/1M tokens)
- “How to use this in your evaluation” checklist
- CTA slide: Try Hosted API / Request Dedicated sizing / Talk to us about Private
- Appendix slide: disclaimer language (backup if needed)

Demo prerequisites
- Benchmark landing page reachable from presenter machine (test from non-corp network)
- Ensure cached responses (avoid cache-miss storm during demo)
- Demo account (if any) prepared; otherwise public page only
- Preloaded fallback:
  - 5 screenshots (filters, chart view, export, methodology section, CTA modal)
  - Local copy of the exported CSV/JSON (for “export” step if export fails)

Required disclaimers (verbatim-ish; Legal approved)
- “All results reflect Redwood-run benchmarks under the configurations described in the methodology. Performance and cost vary by workload, region, model version, and deployment configuration.”
- “Competitor context (if referenced) is directional and may not reflect the latest hardware, pricing, or configurations.”
- “Do not use this webinar as a substitute for validating against your own traffic and prompts.”

---
5) Run of show (minute-by-minute)

Total target: 45 minutes

00:00–02:00 — Welcome + housekeeping (Noura)
- “Thanks for joining.”
- Recording notice
- Where to ask questions (Q&A panel preferred; chat for logistics)
- Disclaimers (1–2 sentences)

02:00–05:00 — Agenda + who this is for (Noura → Soojin)
- Agenda: why latency/$, what we measured, key findings, live demo, Q&A
- Quick audience framing: engineers evaluating inference economics

05:00–13:00 — Why latency/$ + how to interpret the report (Soojin)
Key beats
- Latency alone ≠ user experience; cost alone ≠ scalable product; you need the joint view
- The metric is a decision-support tool, not a trophy metric
- What you’ll learn:
  - Which model+region combos give strong latency/$
  - How p95 and throughput relate to user experience and SLOs
  - How to choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private based on consistency + control

13:00–23:00 — Methodology highlights (Claire)
Must-cover bullets
- Workloads: prefill vs decode mix; prompt sets designed to reflect production distributions
- Concurrency levels and why (avoid single-request cherry-picking)
- Warmup and stability gates (reruns when variance crosses threshold)
- Caching/batching policy: what was enabled/disabled in the published numbers (align to methodology doc)
- Metric definitions:
  - latency/$ (normalization)
  - p50/p95 latency
  - throughput (tokens/sec) and why raw TPS can mislead
- Exclusions + caveats: outlier handling, missing region reruns, capacity constraints

23:00–31:00 — Key results + “how to use this” (Jonas)
- 2–3 takeaways maximum (keep crisp):
  1) Region consistency: what we saw, how to think about it
  2) p95 matters: what changes when you optimize for tail latency
  3) Cost/perf tradeoffs: how small config changes can shift unit economics
- “What should you do next?”
  - Use interactive page to filter to your region/context length
  - Validate with your prompts (we provide reproducibility artifacts)
  - If you need predictability (SLA/residency), talk Dedicated/Private

31:00–38:00 — Live demo (Felix) + assisted narration (Noura keeps time)
Demo goal: prove the page is usable and honest (clear disclaimers, export, methodology)

Demo script (exact clicks)
1) Open landing page at top (10–15s)
   - Point out disclaimer + “How we measured” link
2) Scroll to interactive table (15s)
   - Explain columns: latency/$, p50, p95, $/1M tokens, throughput
3) Filter by:
   - Region: “EU West” (example)
   - Context length bucket: “longer context” (use actual filter names)
   - Model family: pick 2–3 models (don’t spend time debating model list)
4) Toggle metric view (latency/$ ↔ p95) (20s)
   - Explain how rankings can change depending on whether you optimize for tail
5) Open a row details / tooltip (if present) (15s)
   - Call out methodology notes + what config the number corresponds to
6) Export (CSV/JSON) (20s)
   - “This is how you can share internally or rerun analyses.”
7) Show CTAs (10s)
   - Hosted API trial
   - Dedicated sizing
   - Private deployment conversation

Demo fallback plan (if page is slow/429/5xx)
- Switch to screenshot deck immediately (Alicia to provide)
- Verbally confirm “the same functionality is available post-webinar; link will be sent”
- Do not speculate about incident cause; keep it simple (“we’re seeing some load; we’ll use screenshots to keep moving”)

38:00–45:00 — Q&A (Noura moderates; route questions)
- Claire: methodology, fairness, caching, variance
- Jonas: interpretation, what drives differences, p95 vs throughput
- Felix: page usage, export, schema versioning
- Markus: “how to evaluate Redwood for my workload,” PoC steps

Time management
- At 43:30 do final question + closing CTA

---
6) Q&A bank (approved answers + guardrails)

A) Methodology / fairness
Q: “Is this cherry-picked?”
A: “We publish the methodology and the workload definitions, including prompt sets, concurrency, warmups, and stability rules. The goal is reproducibility. You should still validate with your prompts, and we include caveats where performance varies.”

Q: “Did you enable caching/batching?”
A: “We follow a published policy described in the methodology. We’re explicit about what’s enabled so the numbers are interpretable. For production deployments, caching/batching configuration can materially change both latency and cost; we encourage testing with your traffic.”

Q: “Why not show every model?”
A: “We curated a set of commonly used open models and configurations we can support reliably across regions. We’ll expand coverage over time; the interactive page and artifacts are versioned.”

Q: “How many runs / what about variance?”
A: “We run repeated sweeps and apply stability gates; when variance exceeds thresholds we rerun and investigate. We also surface p95 and supporting metrics alongside latency/$.”

B) Comparing providers
Q: “Are you saying Redwood is the best/fastest?”
A: “No. We’re sharing what we measured under specific workloads and configurations. The right choice depends on your workload, region, model, and constraints like residency and SLA.”

Q: “Can I replicate this against another provider?”
A: “Yes in principle; the methodology is documented. You’ll need to align workload definitions, concurrency, and pricing assumptions. We can share guidance for a fair PoC setup.”

C) Practical evaluation / next steps
Q: “What’s the fastest way to see if this matches my product?”
A: “Pick your top 10 prompts and expected concurrency. Start with Hosted API to measure p50/p95 and unit cost. If you need predictable throughput or isolation, we’ll help size Dedicated; for regulated workloads we can discuss Private (VPC/on-prem).”

Q: “What metrics should I care about besides latency/$?”
A: “Tail latency (p95), error rate/retries, throughput under concurrency, and quality/regression behavior for your prompts. Latency/$ is a useful lens but not the only one.”

D) Regions / residency
Q: “Do you support data residency in the EU?”
A: “We can support EU-region deployments; specific options depend on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. For strict residency and network controls, Private/VPC is usually the right starting point.”

E) Legal / safe claims
Q: “Can you share exact competitor pricing/hardware?”
A: “We can’t speak to competitors’ internal configurations beyond public information. We focus on transparent Redwood-run results with clear caveats.”

---
7) Post-webinar follow-up sequence

Owner: Ben Carter (email + nurtures), Grace O’Connor (SDR routing), Markus Klein (SE scheduling)

Assets to include in follow-up
- Recording link
- Slides PDF (optional; if approved)
- Benchmark report landing page
- Methodology link
- PDF report download link
- “How to replicate / PoC checklist” (internal doc → external-friendly version if/when approved)

Email 1 — “Thanks + recording” (send 2 hours after)
Audience: all registrants
Content
- 3 bullets: what we covered
- Links: interactive page + methodology + PDF
- CTA: “Try Hosted API” (primary), “Request Dedicated sizing” (secondary)

Email 2 — “How to apply this to your workload” (T+2 days)
Segments
- PLG/dev: quickstart + sample prompts/eval harness pointers
- Enterprise/regulated: Dedicated/Private consult CTA + residency/security note

Email 3 — “Office hours / ask us anything” (T+7 days)
- Invite to 30-min office hours session
- CTA: book time with Solutions Engineering

SDR/AE tasks (T+1 day)
- For leads with high intent signals (attended live + clicked CTA/export):
  - Route to SDR within 24 hours
  - Suggested opener: “Want us to run your prompt set through the same harness?”

Retargeting / community
- Clip 2 short segments (30–60s) for social:
  1) “Why latency/$” explanation
  2) “How to interpret p95 vs latency/$”
- Post webinar recording to community channels with links to methodology

Measurement (Logan/Tyler)
- Track:
  - Registrations → attendance rate
  - Benchmark page visits from webinar
  - Export clicks
  - CTA clicks (trial/demo/sizing)
  - Influenced pipeline tagging in HubSpot
